items.stem: According to the latest forecast, the pattern of pressure changes near the coast ____ before dawn.

explanation.answer_explanation: The singular head noun pattern takes the singular verb is; the intervening of-phrase does not change the subject.

distractor_rationales.A: Correct: is agrees with the singular subject pattern.
distractor_rationales.B: The plural verb are incorrectly agrees with pressure or changes instead of pattern.
distractor_rationales.C: This is a nonfinite fragment and does not provide a finite main verb.
distractor_rationales.D: This repeats the subject and omits the required finite verb construction after the blank.

taxonomy.subtype: subject-verb agreement across an intervening prepositional phrase

items.stem: The map archivist explained ____ during the survey.

options.A: where had the old boundary markers been moved
options.B: where the old boundary markers had been moved
options.D: where did the old boundary markers move

explanation.answer_explanation: An embedded question uses statement order: subject before the auxiliary, as in where the markers had been moved.

distractor_rationales.A: The auxiliary is inverted as in a direct question, so the embedded clause has the wrong word order.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct: the embedded question has the subject before the auxiliary.
distractor_rationales.C: The embedded clause is incomplete because it lacks a finite verb.
distractor_rationales.D: This uses direct-question inversion inside an embedded question.

taxonomy.subtype: embedded question with statement word order

items.stem: The sandstone tablet, ____ during the excavation, is now displayed in the conservation laboratory.

explanation.answer_explanation: The non-restrictive relative clause needs which as its marker and the passive verb phrase was uncovered.

distractor_rationales.A: What cannot introduce this non-restrictive relative clause.
distractor_rationales.B: Uncovering is the wrong verb form for the required passive predicate.
distractor_rationales.C: Correct: which introduces the clause and was uncovered is passive and finite.
distractor_rationales.D: The relative marker and a redundant subject pronoun duplicate the subject.

taxonomy.subtype: non-restrictive relative clause with passive predicate

items.stem: The telescope records extra images ____ the sky becomes clear after sunset.

explanation.answer_explanation: The time clause requires when followed by a subject and a finite verb: the sky becomes clear.

distractor_rationales.A: During is a preposition and cannot introduce the following finite clause.
distractor_rationales.B: The clause uses a nonfinite form instead of the required finite verb.
distractor_rationales.C: The subject and predicate are incorrectly ordered and the clause is not well formed.
distractor_rationales.D: Correct: when introduces a complete time clause with subject and finite verb.

taxonomy.subtype: time clause introduced by when

items.stem: The alloy remains flexible ____ repeated cooling and heating.

explanation.answer_explanation: Despite correctly introduces the noun phrase repeated cooling and heating to express contrast.

distractor_rationales.A: Correct: despite is followed directly by a noun phrase.
distractor_rationales.B: Although must introduce a finite clause, not the noun phrase that follows.
distractor_rationales.C: In spite requires the preposition of before this noun phrase.
distractor_rationales.D: Despite does not take of; the extra preposition is unnecessary.

taxonomy.subtype: contrast connector before a noun phrase

items.stem: By the time the survey team arrived, the mineral samples ____ in sealed containers.

explanation.answer_explanation: The earlier completed event requires past perfect, and the samples receive the action, so the form is had been labeled.

distractor_rationales.A: The participle is malformed; label must be in its past-participial form.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct: had been labeled is past perfect passive.
distractor_rationales.C: The active form incorrectly makes the samples perform the labeling.
distractor_rationales.D: The passive auxiliary is missing its required past participle.

taxonomy.subtype: past perfect passive before a later past event

items.stem: The monitoring station's new filter made the river water ____ after heavy rainfall.

explanation.answer_explanation: Make takes an object followed by a bare predicate adjective: made the water clearer.

distractor_rationales.A: Correct: clearer is the adjective complement after the object river water.
distractor_rationales.B: Clearly is an adverb, not the required predicate adjective.
distractor_rationales.C: Make does not take to plus the infinitive in this object-complement pattern.
distractor_rationales.D: The -ing form does not function as the required adjective complement here.

taxonomy.subtype: causative verb with object plus predicate adjective

items.stem: ____ in shaded soil, the seeds germinated slowly after the spring rain.

explanation.answer_explanation: The seeds receive the action, so a reduced passive modifier uses the past participle planted.

distractor_rationales.A: Having planting is not a valid perfect participial form.
distractor_rationales.B: The active participle incorrectly presents the seeds as doing the planting.
distractor_rationales.C: Correct: planted is a reduced passive modifier of the seeds.
distractor_rationales.D: Were planted is a finite clause fragment and cannot modify the subject in this position.

taxonomy.subtype: reduced passive participial modifier

items.stem: The detector was ____ to register faint signals from the distant star.

explanation.answer_explanation: Enough follows the adjective in the adjective + enough + to-infinitive construction.

distractor_rationales.A: Enough is placed before the adjective instead of after it.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct: sensitive enough licenses the following to-infinitive.
distractor_rationales.C: So normally requires a that-clause for this result construction.
distractor_rationales.D: The following form is not the required to-infinitive construction.

taxonomy.subtype: adjective plus enough plus to-infinitive result construction

items.stem: During fieldwork, the geologists had to ____ the slope, record the rock layers, and label the samples.

explanation.answer_explanation: Had to is followed by a bare infinitive, and measure is parallel with record and label.

distractor_rationales.A: The -ing form is not the bare infinitive required after had to.
distractor_rationales.B: A noun cannot be coordinated with the two verb forms in the list.
distractor_rationales.C: Correct: measure is the bare infinitive parallel to record and label.
distractor_rationales.D: The added to creates to to measure after had to.

taxonomy.subtype: parallel bare infinitives in a three-part list

items.stem: The museum displayed ____ from the coastal excavation.

options.B: a finely work small bronze bowl
options.C: a finely worked old small bronze bowl
options.D: a finely worked small bronze bowl

explanation.answer_explanation: The participial modifier finely worked precedes the size adjective small, which precedes the material adjective bronze and the noun bowl.

distractor_rationales.A: The modifiers are ordered incorrectly around the participial adjective and material adjective.
distractor_rationales.B: Work is the wrong part-of-speech form; the participial modifier is worked.
distractor_rationales.C: The unnecessary adjective old adds an extraneous element to the planned noun phrase.
distractor_rationales.D: Correct: the modifier order is finely worked, small, bronze, bowl.

taxonomy.subtype: adjective order inside a complex noun phrase

items.stem: Only after the glacier retreated ____ the researchers discover the buried lake.

explanation.answer_explanation: Fronted only after triggers subject-auxiliary inversion: did the researchers discover.

distractor_rationales.A: The inverted auxiliary lacks the required subject.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct: the auxiliary precedes the subject after fronted only after.
distractor_rationales.C: The subject remains before the auxiliary, so inversion is absent.
distractor_rationales.D: This is a nonfinite and incorrectly ordered fragment.

taxonomy.subtype: subject-auxiliary inversion after only after

items.stem: Near the wind-eroded ridge, ____ several narrow channels after the storm.

explanation.answer_explanation: The existential construction uses there, and the plural postposed noun channels requires were.

distractor_rationales.A: Correct: there were agrees with the plural noun channels.
distractor_rationales.B: It is a referring pronoun and does not form the required existential construction.
distractor_rationales.C: The singular verb was does not agree with plural channels.
distractor_rationales.D: The expletive there is missing.

taxonomy.subtype: there plus be with a plural postposed noun phrase

items.stem: The mentor and the apprentice recorded their measurements before ____ submitted the report.

explanation.answer_explanation: The coordinated subjects are plural, so the following subject pronoun is they.

distractor_rationales.A: He is singular and cannot refer to both the mentor and the apprentice.
distractor_rationales.B: Them is an object pronoun, not the subject of submitted.
distractor_rationales.C: Correct: they is the plural subject pronoun for the two people.
distractor_rationales.D: Their is possessive and cannot function as the subject here.

taxonomy.subtype: plural pronoun reference for a coordinated human subject

items.stem: The accuracy of the experiment depends on ____ of the instrument before each trial.

explanation.answer_explanation: The preposition on requires a noun phrase, and the noun calibration is the head of the phrase.

distractor_rationales.A: A verb phrase cannot serve as the required noun object of on in this construction.
distractor_rationales.B: The noun and adjective are in the wrong order.
distractor_rationales.C: The noun head calibration is missing.
distractor_rationales.D: Correct: the careful calibration is a complete noun phrase after on.

taxonomy.subtype: noun required as the object of a preposition

items.sentence: The calibration of the instruments record stable readings during each trial.

marked_parts.A: The calibration of the instruments record

explanation.answer_explanation: Calibration is the singular head of the subject noun phrase, so the main verb must be records.

taxonomy.subtype: singular head noun in an of-phrase subject

items.sentence: The engineer selected several durability bearings for the test rig.

explanation.answer_explanation: The noun bearings needs an adjective modifier, so durable, not the noun durability, is required.

taxonomy.subtype: adjective required before a plural head noun

items.sentence: Yesterday, after the lighthouse crew had repaired the lamp, the keeper records the inspection details.

marked_parts.A: Yesterday, after the lighthouse crew had repaired the lamp,

explanation.answer_explanation: The explicit past-time adverb Yesterday and the past perfect subordinate clause establish a completed past narrative, so the main verb must be the simple past recorded.

taxonomy.subtype: simple past main verb after a past perfect subordinate clause

items.sentence: The archivist was deeply interested on maps from the coastal archive.

marked_parts.D: on maps from the coastal archive.

explanation.answer_explanation: The established adjective-preposition collocation is interested in, not interested on.

taxonomy.subtype: adjective-governed preposition in an interested-in phrase

items.sentence: The workshop focuses on carve wood and shaping clay for architectural models.

explanation.answer_explanation: The preposition on takes gerund complements, and carving must be parallel with shaping.

taxonomy.subtype: gerund complements coordinated after a training preposition

items.sentence: The engineer is responsible to the mountain station's ventilation system.

explanation.answer_explanation: When responsible means having duty for something, it is followed by the preposition for.

taxonomy.subtype: adjective complement after responsible for

items.sentence: The museum restored a bronze finely decorated vessel from the collection.

explanation.answer_explanation: The participial modifier finely decorated precedes the material adjective bronze in the noun phrase.
explanation.minimal_correction: bronze finely decorated vessel → finely decorated bronze vessel

taxonomy.subtype: participial adjective before a material adjective in a noun phrase

items.sentence: The collection of oral histories contain vivid accounts of migration from the valley.

marked_parts.A: The collection of oral histories contain

explanation.answer_explanation: The singular head noun collection controls agreement; the plural noun histories is inside an of-phrase.

taxonomy.subtype: singular head noun with an of-phrase interrupter

items.sentence: Although the route was steep, but the hikers reached the summit before noon.

explanation.answer_explanation: Although already introduces the subordinate contrast clause, so the additional coordinator but is unnecessary.

taxonomy.subtype: removal of a redundant coordinator after an although clause

items.sentence: The manuscript was carefully restored the librarian last year.

explanation.answer_explanation: In the passive construction, the agent must be introduced by by: restored by the librarian.
explanation.minimal_correction: restored the librarian → restored by the librarian

taxonomy.subtype: passive transitive verb requiring a by-agent phrase

items.sentence: The team has carefully prepared the samples that they have record.

explanation.answer_explanation: The auxiliary have requires the past participle recorded.

taxonomy.subtype: past participle after a perfect auxiliary

items.sentence: The lecturer presented a scientifically overview of public water systems.

explanation.answer_explanation: The noun overview requires the adjective scientific as its modifier, not the adverb scientifically.

taxonomy.subtype: adjective required as a noun modifier after an article

items.sentence: The northern route is considerably more shorter than the southern route during winter.

marked_parts.C: more shorter than the southern route

explanation.answer_explanation: Shorter is already a comparative form, so the redundant more must be removed.

taxonomy.subtype: comparative adjective without a redundant more marker

items.sentence: The plants grew slowly during the trial because of the soil remained unusually cold.

marked_parts.D: of the soil remained unusually cold.

explanation.answer_explanation: A finite clause follows because, whereas because of must be followed by a noun phrase.
explanation.minimal_correction: because of the soil remained unusually cold → because the soil remained unusually cold

taxonomy.subtype: because clause rather than because-of before a finite clause

items.sentence: There is several balconies along the theater's upper gallery.

explanation.answer_explanation: The plural postposed noun balconies requires the plural form are in the existential construction.

taxonomy.subtype: there-be agreement with a plural postposed noun phrase

items.sentence: The analyst could not determine why did the values change after calibration.

explanation.answer_explanation: The clause after determine is an embedded question and therefore uses statement order.
explanation.minimal_correction: why did the values change → why the values changed

taxonomy.subtype: embedded why-question with statement word order

items.sentence: The strength of the coating is dependent of temperature and humidity.

explanation.answer_explanation: The established collocation is dependent on, so of is the wrong preposition.

taxonomy.subtype: adjective-governed dependent-on preposition

items.sentence: The committee recommends mapping the district and to revise its zoning plan.

explanation.answer_explanation: The complements coordinated after recommends should be parallel gerund phrases: mapping and revising.

taxonomy.subtype: gerund coordination after recommends

items.sentence: The seedlings grew rapid under the controlled lamps.

explanation.answer_explanation: The verb grew requires the adverb rapidly to describe how the seedlings grew.

taxonomy.subtype: adverb required to modify a verb

items.sentence: The panels, having built from recycled glass, were tested for strength.

explanation.answer_explanation: The panels receive the action, so the reduced modifier must be passive: built from recycled glass.
explanation.minimal_correction: having built from recycled glass → built from recycled glass

taxonomy.subtype: reduced passive modifier before a finite passive predicate

items.sentence: Last year, after the bridge had been inspected, engineers approves the repair plan.

marked_parts.A: Last year, after the bridge had been inspected,

explanation.answer_explanation: The explicit past-time adverb Last year and the past perfect passive clause establish a completed past narrative, so the main verb must be the simple past approved.

taxonomy.subtype: simple past main verb after a past perfect passive clause

items.sentence: The seedlings grew surprising quickly in the greenhouse.

explanation.answer_explanation: The word modifies the adverb quickly, so it must be the adverb surprisingly.

taxonomy.subtype: adverb required to modify an adverb

items.stem: During the severe drought of 2019, the leaves of the desert plant ___.

explanation.answer_explanation: The dated past-time context requires the simple past verb wilted; the plural subject leaves takes the plural-compatible form.

distractor_rationales.A: The present-tense form does not fit the dated past-time context.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct: wilted is the simple past finite verb required by the 2019 context and agrees with plural leaves.
distractor_rationales.C: The singular present form does not agree with plural leaves and does not fit the past-time context.
distractor_rationales.D: The -ing form cannot serve as the finite verb without an auxiliary.

taxonomy.subtype: subject-verb agreement across an intervening prepositional phrase

items.stem: Researchers have not determined ___ the ancient temple was built.

explanation.answer_explanation: An embedded question uses statement order: when the temple was built.

distractor_rationales.A: Inversion is not used in an embedded question.
distractor_rationales.B: Do-inversion is not used after determined.
distractor_rationales.C: Correct: when introduces the embedded clause with statement order.
distractor_rationales.D: That cannot introduce this embedded question meaningfully.

taxonomy.subtype: embedded question with statement word order

items.stem: The proposal was expensive, ___ the council approved it.

explanation.answer_explanation: But correctly coordinates two contrasting independent clauses.

distractor_rationales.A: Correct: but signals the contrast.
distractor_rationales.B: Because gives a cause and cannot coordinate these ideas as intended.
distractor_rationales.C: Unless introduces a condition.
distractor_rationales.D: So that introduces purpose or result.

taxonomy.subtype: contrast connector followed by a finite clause

items.stem: The new trees will make the avenue ___.

explanation.answer_explanation: Make takes an object followed by a predicate adjective describing it.

distractor_rationales.A: The bare noun/verb form is not the required predicate adjective.
distractor_rationales.B: The participle does not fit the selected complement frame.
distractor_rationales.C: Correct: shady is the predicate adjective after make the avenue.
distractor_rationales.D: This adverb cannot function as the predicate complement.

taxonomy.subtype: causative verb followed by object and predicate adjective

items.stem: The chamber produced ___ loud echo that the recording equipment had to be recalibrated.

explanation.answer_explanation: The pattern such a + adjective + singular count noun correctly introduces the result clause: such a loud echo that ...

distractor_rationales.A: Correct: such a precedes the adjective and singular count noun in the result construction.
distractor_rationales.B: So cannot directly precede an article in this position.
distractor_rationales.C: Very cannot directly precede an article in this position.
distractor_rationales.D: As a does not form the required degree expression licensing this result clause.

taxonomy.subtype: such a plus adjective plus singular count noun licensing a result that-clause

items.stem: The exhibit not only informs visitors but also ___.

explanation.answer_explanation: The two coordinated complements are parallel finite verb phrases.

distractor_rationales.A: Correct: entertains them parallels informs visitors.
distractor_rationales.B: The participle is not parallel to the finite verb.
distractor_rationales.C: A noun is not parallel to the verb phrase.
distractor_rationales.D: The infinitive is not parallel to the finite verb.

taxonomy.subtype: not only plus coordinated parallel verb phrases

items.stem: Maya Chen, ___, presented the findings at the conference.

explanation.answer_explanation: The appositive noun phrase follows the proper name and identifies Maya Chen.

distractor_rationales.A: The adjective is misplaced after the noun in this phrase.
distractor_rationales.B: The word order does not form an appositive noun phrase.
distractor_rationales.C: Correct: a respected sociolinguist is a well-formed appositive.
distractor_rationales.D: The determiner and noun order is incorrect.

taxonomy.subtype: appositive noun phrase after a proper noun

items.stem: There ___ several underground streams beneath the valley.

explanation.answer_explanation: The plural postposed noun phrase streams requires are.

distractor_rationales.A: Is does not agree with the plural noun phrase.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct: are agrees with several streams.
distractor_rationales.C: The bare form cannot be the finite verb here.
distractor_rationales.D: The participle cannot serve as the finite verb.

taxonomy.subtype: there plus be with a postposed plural noun phrase

items.stem: The report provides ___ information about regional employment trends.

explanation.answer_explanation: Information is uncountable, so much is the appropriate quantifier.

distractor_rationales.A: Correct: much modifies the uncountable noun information.
distractor_rationales.B: Many modifies plural count nouns.
distractor_rationales.C: Few modifies plural count nouns.
distractor_rationales.D: Several modifies plural count nouns.

taxonomy.subtype: quantifier selected for an uncountable academic noun

items.stem: The filter operates ___ when the input signal contains background noise.

explanation.answer_explanation: An adverb is required to modify the finite verb operates.

distractor_rationales.A: The adjective cannot directly modify operates.
distractor_rationales.B: The noun cannot modify the verb.
distractor_rationales.C: Correct: efficiently is the adverb modifying operates.
distractor_rationales.D: The comparative adjective lacks a comparison and the required adverbial function.

taxonomy.subtype: adverb required to modify a following finite verb

items.stem: The orbit of several newly discovered planets ___ unusually stable.

explanation.answer_explanation: The singular head noun orbit requires the singular verb remains.

distractor_rationales.A: Remain agrees with the nearby plural noun planets, not the subject head.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct: orbit is singular.
distractor_rationales.C: The participle cannot serve as the finite predicate.
distractor_rationales.D: Has remain uses an incorrect participle form.

taxonomy.subtype: subject-verb agreement across an intervening prepositional phrase

items.stem: Researchers are uncertain whether the pottery fragments ___ from the coastal settlement.

explanation.answer_explanation: An embedded whether-question uses statement word order: subject followed by the finite verb.

distractor_rationales.A: Inversion with did is not used in this embedded question.
distractor_rationales.B: The auxiliary is misplaced and the clause is ungrammatical.
distractor_rationales.C: Correct: the fragments originated there.
distractor_rationales.D: This is not a complete finite clause.

taxonomy.subtype: embedded question with noninverted word order

items.stem: The researcher cataloged the fern species ___ the expedition had collected.

explanation.answer_explanation: That correctly introduces a restrictive relative clause and functions as its object.

distractor_rationales.A: Correct: that is the object of had collected.
distractor_rationales.B: What cannot follow an antecedent noun in this construction.
distractor_rationales.C: They creates an extra subject and leaves the object missing.
distractor_rationales.D: Which them contains a redundant object.

taxonomy.subtype: restrictive relative pronoun as object

items.stem: If the city ___ the subsidy, more households would install efficient heating systems.

explanation.answer_explanation: The second conditional uses a simple past form in the if-clause and would plus base verb in the result.

distractor_rationales.A: The present tense does not form the intended second conditional.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct: increased pairs with would install.
distractor_rationales.C: Will is not normally used in this if-clause.
distractor_rationales.D: The progressive form is not required and changes the construction.

taxonomy.subtype: second conditional clause with full subordinate-clause structure

items.stem: ___ its low density, the alloy withstands considerable pressure.

explanation.answer_explanation: Despite is followed directly by a noun phrase and expresses concession.

distractor_rationales.A: Although requires a finite clause, not this noun phrase.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct: despite its low density.
distractor_rationales.C: Despite of is not the standard prepositional form.
distractor_rationales.D: Because expresses cause rather than concession.

taxonomy.subtype: concessive relation requiring a prepositional connector before a noun phrase

items.stem: The storm system ___ by satellite instruments before it reached the coast.

explanation.answer_explanation: The system receives the action, so the finite passive was tracked is required.

distractor_rationales.A: Was tracking gives the subject an agentive meaning.
distractor_rationales.B: Tracked is active and lacks an expressed agent.
distractor_rationales.C: Correct: the system was tracked.
distractor_rationales.D: Tracking is a nonfinite fragment here.

taxonomy.subtype: passive voice in a finite main clause

items.stem: The new park design made the narrow corridor ___ and safer for pedestrians.

explanation.answer_explanation: Make takes an object followed by a bare adjective complement; wider is coordinated with safer.

distractor_rationales.A: Make does not take a to-infinitive complement in this frame.
distractor_rationales.B: The participle is not parallel with safer.
distractor_rationales.C: Widened suggests a passive result and is not coordinated with safer.
distractor_rationales.D: Correct: made the corridor wider and safer.

taxonomy.subtype: causative make followed by object and adjective complement

items.stem: The fibers ___ with a protective coating retain their strength after repeated washing and drying.

explanation.answer_explanation: Treated is a reduced passive relative clause modifying fibers: fibers that were treated.

distractor_rationales.A: Correct: treated means that were treated.
distractor_rationales.B: Treating gives the fibers an incorrect active role.
distractor_rationales.C: Were treated creates a second finite verb in the noun phrase.
distractor_rationales.D: Having treat has an incorrect participle form.

taxonomy.subtype: reduced passive relative clause with a past participle

items.stem: The software not only records performances but also ___ background noise automatically.

explanation.answer_explanation: Not only records but also filters coordinates two finite verbs with the same subject.

distractor_rationales.A: Filtering is not parallel with the finite verb records.
distractor_rationales.B: The to-infinitive is not parallel with records.
distractor_rationales.C: Correct: records and filters are coordinated finite verbs.
distractor_rationales.D: The past tense breaks the intended present-tense coordination.

taxonomy.subtype: not only but also with coordinated finite verbs

items.stem: Had the reef restoration project ___ earlier, the damaged habitat might have recovered before winter.

explanation.answer_explanation: Had plus the past participle forms an inverted past-perfect conditional: had begun.

distractor_rationales.A: Correct: had begun is the inverted form of if the project had begun.
distractor_rationales.B: Beginning cannot follow had.
distractor_rationales.C: The inverted clause does not take an extra subject it.
distractor_rationales.D: Been begin uses an incorrect participle.

taxonomy.subtype: elliptical conditional inversion with had

items.stem: There ___ several blank areas on the early map of the northern coast.

explanation.answer_explanation: The plural postverbal noun phrase areas requires are in this existential construction.

distractor_rationales.A: Is is singular and does not agree with areas.
distractor_rationales.B: Correct: there are several blank areas.
distractor_rationales.C: Being is nonfinite.
distractor_rationales.D: Has does not form the existential construction here.

taxonomy.subtype: there plus be with a plural postverbal noun phrase

items.stem: The recipe requires ___ additional information about the nutritional content of the grain.

explanation.answer_explanation: Information is uncountable, so some is the compatible quantifier.

distractor_rationales.A: Many modifies countable plural nouns.
distractor_rationales.B: Few also modifies countable plural nouns.
distractor_rationales.C: Correct: some information.
distractor_rationales.D: Several requires a countable plural noun.

taxonomy.subtype: quantifier compatible with an uncountable noun

items.stem: The archivist explained that the fragile documents must be handled ___ during the transfer.

explanation.answer_explanation: Carefully is the adverb modifying handled.

distractor_rationales.A: Careful is an adjective, not the required adverb.
distractor_rationales.B: Carefulness is a noun.
distractor_rationales.C: Care is a noun or verb and cannot modify handled here.
distractor_rationales.D: Correct: handled carefully.

taxonomy.subtype: adverb required to modify a finite verb

items.sentence: A architect measured the vaulted entrance before the renovation began.

explanation.answer_explanation: The consonant letter a is pronounced with an initial vowel sound, so the article must be an.

taxonomy.subtype: indefinite article before a consonant-initial noun

items.sentence: The region experienced a dramatically temperature shift during the afternoon.

explanation.answer_explanation: Dramatic is the adjective required to modify temperature; dramatically is an adverb.

taxonomy.subtype: adjective required before a head noun

items.sentence: The clinic introduced the screening program after it identify the main risk factors.

explanation.answer_explanation: The completed past event requires the simple past identified.

taxonomy.subtype: simple past finite verb in a completed historical sequence

items.sentence: The course emphasizes reading technical articles, analyzing evidence, and to present findings clearly.

explanation.answer_explanation: The three complements after emphasizes must use parallel gerund forms.

taxonomy.subtype: parallel gerund complements in a coordinated list

items.sentence: The agency is responsible of monitoring water quality near the reservoir.

explanation.answer_explanation: The adjective responsible takes the fixed preposition for before its gerund complement.

taxonomy.subtype: adjective complement with the fixed preposition responsible for

items.sentence: The buses that travels along the old route carry commuters into the city each morning.

explanation.answer_explanation: The relative-clause subject that refers to the plural noun buses, so the finite verb must be travel.

taxonomy.subtype: subject-verb agreement with a plural subject

items.sentence: Despite the market was unstable, investors continued to purchase municipal bonds.

explanation.answer_explanation: A finite clause requires although, whereas despite must be followed by a noun phrase or gerund.

taxonomy.subtype: although introducing a finite concessive clause

items.sentence: The plant is one of the species with whom the botanist has worked for years.

marked_parts.D: the botanist has worked for years

explanation.answer_explanation: Which refers to the plant species; whom is used for people.

taxonomy.subtype: relative pronoun as the object of a preposition

items.sentence: The pattern of clouds over the mountain indicate an approaching storm.

explanation.answer_explanation: The singular head noun pattern requires indicates.

taxonomy.subtype: subject-verb agreement across an intervening modifier

items.sentence: Only much of the dietary samples contained enough iron for the analysis.

explanation.answer_explanation: Samples is a countable plural noun, so many, not much, is required.

taxonomy.subtype: quantifier compatible with a countable plural noun

items.sentence: The lecturer discussed the historical develop of the regional dialect.

explanation.answer_explanation: The premodifier historical requires the noun development as the head of the phrase.

taxonomy.subtype: noun required as the head of a prepositional object

items.sentence: The components were assembling in a sealed chamber to prevent contamination.

explanation.answer_explanation: The components receive the action, so be must be followed by the passive participle assembled.

taxonomy.subtype: passive participle after a finite form of be

items.sentence: The committee reviewed the proposal and approving the revised budget after the public hearing.

marked_parts.D: the revised budget after the public hearing

explanation.answer_explanation: The coordinated predicates share the past-tense subject committee, so reviewed and approved must be parallel finite verbs.

taxonomy.subtype: parallel finite verbs in a coordinated predicate

items.sentence: The analyst succeeded in predict the quarterly trend despite limited data.

explanation.answer_explanation: The preposition in takes a gerund complement, predicting.

taxonomy.subtype: gerund as the complement of a preposition

items.sentence: The eastern plateau is high than the valley during the dry season.

explanation.answer_explanation: Than requires the comparative form higher.

taxonomy.subtype: comparative adjective required by than

items.sentence: The archivist cataloged several traditional tale from the mountain region.

explanation.answer_explanation: The quantifier several requires a countable plural noun, so tale must be changed to tales.

taxonomy.subtype: plural noun after a plural quantifier

items.sentence: The amendment appears in constitutional after the court's review.

explanation.answer_explanation: Appear takes the predicate adjective directly; the inserted preposition in is not part of the linking-verb frame.

taxonomy.subtype: predicate adjective after a linking verb

items.sentence: The librarian organized the archived manuscripts methodical.

explanation.answer_explanation: The verb organized is modified by the adverb methodically, not the adjective methodical.

taxonomy.subtype: adverb required to modify a research verb

items.sentence: The volunteers collected water samples monitor pollution levels in the wetland.

explanation.answer_explanation: The infinitive marker to is required before the purpose verb monitor.

taxonomy.subtype: infinitive of purpose after a finite verb

items.sentence: The observatory benefits from clear skies and benefits to precise measurements.

explanation.answer_explanation: Benefit takes the preposition from when it means to gain an advantage from something.

taxonomy.subtype: fixed preposition collocation after benefit

items.sentence: The conductor rehearsed the ensemble and checking the balance of the brass section.

marked_parts.D: the balance of the brass section

explanation.answer_explanation: Rehearsed and checked are coordinated finite past-tense verbs with the same subject.

taxonomy.subtype: parallel finite verbs in a coordinated predicate

items.sentence: Each of the historic vehicles require careful maintenance.

explanation.answer_explanation: The subject each is singular, so the verb must be requires.

taxonomy.subtype: singular agreement after each

items.sentence: The treatment plant replaced a concrete ancient pipe beneath the filtration basin.

explanation.answer_explanation: In this noun phrase, the age adjective ancient precedes the material adjective concrete, and the article changes to an.

taxonomy.subtype: adjective order inside a noun phrase
